skill.name: animate
skill.description: Build accessible, purposeful interface animations from scratch. Choose whether motion is needed, then select the tool, properties, timing, interruption behavior, exit, reduced-motion treatment, and implementation.
skill.summary: Create purposeful UI motion with clear decisions for tools, timing, performance, and accessibility.
skill.author: emilkowalski

security_audit.summary: All 47 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, prose, CSS and JavaScript examples, or a documentation link. The reviewed files provide animation guidance and implementation recipes, with no evidence of shell execution, reconnaissance, unauthorized networking, prompt injection, or data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Static analysis treats Markdown code formatting and JavaScript template literals as shell execution.
remediation.suggestion: Refine the scanner to distinguish Ruby shell backticks from Markdown backticks and JavaScript template literals.

remediation.issue: Static analysis flags ordinary animation guidance as system or network reconnaissance.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict reconnaissance rules to host or network inspection APIs and exclude prose, CSS examples, and design terminology.

remediation.issue: The skill links to external easing references.
remediation.suggestion: Keep external links informational and document that the skill does not fetch them or require network access.

content.value_statement: Unfocused motion can slow interfaces, distract users, and create accessibility problems. This skill selects purposeful techniques and writes implementation guidance for responsive, maintainable animations.
actual_capabilities: Decides whether an interaction needs animation based on frequency and purpose.
Selects CSS transitions, CSS animations, WAAPI, or Motion for a requested effect.
Recommends transform, opacity, easing, duration, and spring settings.
Accounts for interruption, exit direction, hover capability, and pointer behavior.
Includes reduced-motion guidance and implementation examples.
Writes concise animation code for common interface patterns.
limitations: It does not inspect or modify an existing codebase without relevant files and context.
It does not replace visual testing on real devices or varied performance conditions.
It does not design complete components or focus management; use a component skill when needed.
Timing recommendations may require adjustment for the product context and brand.

use_cases.title: Polish a Frontend Interaction
use_cases.description: Add a responsive transition to a button, menu, modal, toast, or tab indicator with clear timing and reduced-motion behavior.

use_cases.title: Set a Motion System
use_cases.description: Create consistent easing, duration, transform, and interruption rules for a product interface.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a Motion Decision
use_cases.description: Decide whether a proposed effect supports feedback, spatial consistency, state indication, explanation, or delight.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Simple Transition
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a subtle hover and press animation to this button. Choose the properties, curve, duration, and reduced-motion behavior. Return the implementation and a brief rationale.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Menu
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an entrance and exit animation for this dropdown. Preserve the trigger origin, support interruption, gate hover behavior, and include accessible reduced-motion handling.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Right Motion Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the animation for this interaction. Decide whether CSS, WAAPI, or Motion is the cheapest suitable tool, then provide the implementation with timing and performance reasoning.

prompt_templates.title: Define a Motion Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this interaction request and decide whether it should animate. Name the purpose, frequency tier, properties, curve, duration or spring, interruption behavior, exit behavior, and feel checks before writing the code.

output_examples.input: Add a transition for a search panel that opens from a toolbar button.
output_examples.output: A compact implementation using opacity and transform, anchored to the button, with a short ease-out curve and a reduced-motion variant.

output_examples.input: Should a command palette animate when opened by a keyboard shortcut?
output_examples.output: No animation. The interaction is frequent and keyboard initiated, so an immediate state change improves speed and predictability.
A gesture-aware implementation using a spring, pointer capture, velocity and distance thresholds, symmetric dismissal, and touch-safe behavior.

best_practices: Name the interaction purpose before choosing an animation.
Prefer transform and opacity, then verify behavior with reduced-motion settings.
Test interruption, exit behavior, touch input, and perceived timing on real devices.
anti_patterns: Adding motion to frequent keyboard actions without a clear user benefit.
Using transition: all, scale(0), or long UI durations without a specific reason.
Shipping hover motion without pointer gating or reduced-motion support.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates purposeful interface animation implementations with decisions for tools, properties, timing, interruption, exit, and accessibility.

faq.question: Which animation technologies does it use?
faq.answer: It chooses among CSS transitions, CSS animations, the Web Animations API, and Motion based on the interaction.

faq.question: Can it decide that no animation is better?
faq.answer: Yes. Frequent or keyboard-initiated actions may work better with an immediate state change.

faq.question: Does it support accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes reduced-motion behavior and pointer gating when those controls are relevant.

faq.question: Can it build complete UI components?
faq.answer: It focuses on motion. Use a component-focused skill for focus management, semantics, and complete interaction behavior.

faq.question: How should I validate the result?
faq.answer: Check the motion at different speeds, inspect frames, test interruption and gestures, and verify reduced-motion behavior on real devices.
